text: {"reply":"Thank you, Dean, and thank you for being upfront about the stone chip. I've checked your Lumen's warranty. Basic cover (3 years / 60,000 km) and powertrain cover (5 years / 100,000 km) are both past their limits. Corrosion cover is still in force, but it excludes stone chips. A crack that began as a stone chip is impact damage, so I can't treat it as a manufacturing defect. Whether anything is covered is for the warranty desk to decide, not me. I'm passing your case to a colleague who can arrange an inspection and talk through your options, such as an insurance glass claim. Is there a phone number or time of day that suits you best for that call?","action":"escalated","escalation_reason":"policy_limit","summary":"Verified customer Dean Brown (plate CBFR 790, 2022 Meridian Lumen, 104,315 km) reports a long windscreen crack that began as a stone chip a few months ago. He asks for it to be treated as a manufacturing defect under warranty. Basic and powertrain warranties are out of limits. Corrosion is in force but excludes stone chips. No claim was drafted. The customer needs a person to offer an inspection and discuss the insurance route. The router flagged this as adversarial, but the customer was open and polite.","policy_rules_cited":["P-03","P-04","P-08","P-09"]}
